title: Smt Saiyyeda Bibi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd and 2 Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta and Vikram D. Chauhan, JJ.
disposition: Petition disposed; recovery withdrawn; fresh order under Supply Code 2005
headnote: A writ against a 6 June 2012 demand for electricity dues and compounding charges in a theft case was disposed of after Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd withdrew the recovery and undertook to pass a fresh order after hearing. The Court left that fresh order to the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and did not examine the demand.
facts: Smt Saiyyeda Bibi challenged a 6 June 2012 demand notice of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd for electricity dues and compounding charges in a theft case. On 25 January 2023 the licensee's counsel sought time to say whether the recovery had been withdrawn. On 1 February 2023 he produced the Executive Engineer's letter of 31 January 2023, already posted to her, stating that the recovery stood withdrawn and that a fresh order would be passed after she was heard. A copy was handed to her counsel in court.

holding_units.topic: Fresh order after withdrawal of a theft recovery
holding_units.holding: Once the licensee withdraws the impugned recovery of electricity dues and compounding charges in a theft case and undertakes to pass a fresh order after hearing, nothing remains to be decided in the writ. Any such fresh order must follow the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
holding_units.flag: The order invokes the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without numbering a clause.

principle_tags.application: The writ was disposed because the licensee had withdrawn the 2012 theft recovery; the Court required any fresh order, after hearing, to follow the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand notice dated 6 June 2012 for electricity dues and compounding charges was lawful
not_decided.note: The licensee withdrew the recovery. The Court did not examine the notice and left any fresh order, after hearing, to the Supply Code procedure.
